issue_context.title: DOC: Wrong Series.rename parameter documentation
issue_context.body:
### Pandas version checks

- [X] I have checked that the issue still exists on the latest versions of the docs on `main` [here](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/dev/)


### Location of the documentation

https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/reference/api/pandas.Series.rename.html

### Documentation problem

Documentation says only `inplace` keyword is used, but actually other keywords from `DataFrame.rename` are valid

- `copy`

```python
import pandas as pd

s = pd.Series(["foo", "bar"])
shallow = s.rename({1: 9}, copy=False)
s[0] = "foobar"

print(s)
# 0    foobar
# 1       bar
# dtype: object

print(shallow)
# 0    foobar
# 9       bar
# dtype: object
```

- `errors`
```python
import pandas as pd

s = pd.Series(["foo", "bar"])
s.rename({2: 9}, errors="raise")  # This raises
```

- `level`
```python
import pandas as pd

arrays = [
    ["bar", "bar", "baz", "baz"],
    ["one", "two", "baz", "baz"],
]
tuples = list(zip(*arrays))
index = pd.MultiIndex.from_tuples(tuples, names=["first", "second"])
s = pd.Series([0, 1, 2, 3], index=index)

print(s)
# first  second
# bar    one       0
#        two       1
# baz    baz       2
#        baz       3
# dtype: int64

print(s.rename({"baz": "buz"}, level=1))
# first  second
# bar    one       0
#        two       1
# baz    buz       2
#        buz       3
# dtype: int64
```

### Suggested fix for documentation

Document the above args - or just mention `Series.rename` accepts all args of `DataFrame.rename` except `labels` and `columns`
